newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on technicals, firm cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on technicals, firm cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures staged a late rally Tuesday and ended up sharply in moderate trade, driven by some technical buying and reports of further strength in the cash, industry sources said.
June rallied 8.9 cents to close at $2.309 per million British thermal units. July settled 8.1 cents higher at $2.338. Others ended up by 2.5 to 7.6 cents.

"Cash was better bid this morning and that's what caused the screen to move up early. Then, locals bid it up late when they didn't see any big sell paper," said one Texas-based trader, noting firm winter futures also helped fuel the rally.

"What dazzles me is how strong the winter months are which is giving people a reason to buy prompt," he said, adding he remained skeptical current prices could be sustained without broader cooling loads.
Weather forecasts this week were mixed, calling for hot temperatures in the western U.S., while the East and Midwest were expected to range between normal and slightly below-normal.

Technical traders agreed the market was overbought after an 11 percent rally in six sessions and due for a correction. They now pegged resistance in June in the $2.33 area and then at the $2.385 contract high. Support was first seen at $2.20, with major buying likely at $2.05 and then along the up trendline in the $2.03 area.

In the cash, steady injection demand helped boost Gulf Coast swing prices by a couple of cents Tuesday to the low-$2.20s, with gas at Henry Hub talked in the mid-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas firmed a nickel to the low-$2.50s or better.
Early expectations for Wednesday's weekly AGA inventory report call for a build in the 25-70 bcf range versus a gain of 53 bcf a year ago.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip jumped 6.4 cents to $2.364. NYMEX said 42,752 contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 35,331.

On the KCBT, June finished seven cents higher at $2.13, while deferreds ended up by five to seven cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.9 cents to 17.9 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 187 lots changed hands, down from Monday's total of 405.
